A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, proofs, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched despite substantial rewriting, renaming, and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 Section 5 and Appendices C–D report original training, certification, and sensitivity results on CIFAR-10, Imagenette, ImageNet, and HAM10k.

after.justification: v3 Section 6 and Appendix D report original benchmark and medical-image evaluations, including unequal-cost comparisons and additional diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: v3 substantially revises the training objective: cost-weighted sums of target-specific radius losses replace v2's group-radius sensitive loss, with separate loss weights. The sensitive margin interval changes from [-γ2,γ2] to [0,γ2], and the accuracy loss is expressed over noise-augmented base-classifier predictions (v2 Section 4 versus v3 Equation 4).

E1.justification: The four datasets and classification domains remain. v3 adds unequal-cost CIFAR-10 scenarios and changes HAM10k from malignant-to-benign errors alone incurring cost to a 10:1 cost ratio covering both error directions. The additional seed-class sweep summarized in v2 Table 9 is removed.

E2.justification: After matching the -R and -CS names, v3 adds SmoothMix and its adaptation to HAM10k and ImageNet comparisons and expands the Zhang & Evans comparison to include smoothing baselines. SmoothMix's adaptation also substantively changes: v2 Appendix B reweights the mixup loss, whereas v3 Equation 14 reweights the natural loss.

E3.justification: v3 adds certified robust cost and medical precision/recall metrics and redesigns the Zhang & Evans comparison, reporting common training/testing noise σ=0.25 instead of v2's comparison at unequal perturbation bounds. The stated ImageNet architecture changes from ResNet-50 to ResNet-18. These are reported protocol changes; they do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a loss-weight sensitivity study (Table 7) and radius-distribution analyses for sensitive, normal, and all samples (Figures 3(a) and 7–9). It removes v2's direct accuracy–robustness trade-off comparisons and averaged cost-matrix analysis. The margin-threshold grid, varying-noise evaluations, and classwise error heatmaps remain.

E5.justification: v2 Table 9 reports averaged scores with ± terms across sensitive-class and target-set selections. v3 removes this summary without replacement variability reporting. These are averages across scenarios, not documented repeated-training-seed statistics.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive robust-cost results, unequal-cost comparisons, medical precision/recall, and new analysis outcomes. For CIFAR-10 S-Seed, reported (Acc, Robcs) changes from (66.1%, 62.8%) for Ours to (67.5%, 54.8%) for the revised Margin-CS; several baseline values also change. Many ImageNet entries and the heatmap values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 extends binary costs to nonnegative real costs, introduces a formal pairwise radius and weighted robust-cost definition, and expands the radius-ordering and confidence theorems with corresponding proofs. It also explicitly sets all radii to zero for incorrect predictions, whereas v2's cost-sensitive certificate could cover misclassifications that incurred no cost.

C1.justification: The abstract's certification scope expands from any binary cost matrix to any cost matrix, accompanied by weighted robust-cost optimization as a central contribution. v3 also positions the work as a broader framework encompassing adaptive training approaches, while retaining the main accuracy–cost-sensitive-robustness trade-off claim.

C2.justification: New Appendix C discusses control versus flexibility and tightness versus scalability, including worst-case quadratic dependence on label count and mitigation through sparse cost matrices. v3 adds medical imbalance/recall interpretations and numerical-stability explanations. The earlier rationale for optimizing negative-radius sensitive samples disappears, while the cat–dog error trade-off discussion remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds substantial documentation of hard versus soft smoothing, mixup construction and gradient handling, dataset sizes and preprocessing, and explicit loss-weight defaults. The reported code location changes from TrustMLRG/CS-RS to AppleXY/Cost-Sensitive-RS. Hardware and runtime disclosures largely remain, but the earlier explicit Imagenette architecture specification is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands research positioning through separate discussions of certification approaches and standard/adversarial cost-sensitive learning. Added citations include verification and cost-sensitive-learning works such as Katz et al., Kukar et al., and Zadrozny et al. The Wang et al. citation supporting optimization of misclassified examples is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, training explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work becomes a separate section, adversarial-robustness background is added, and the appendices are reorganized around notation, certification, discussion, and experiments. The title, author list, and method terminology also change.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column conference layout and reorganizes benchmark tables by dataset, adding robust-cost columns and highlighted method rows. It adds conceptual certification illustrations and radius-distribution figures, redraws the robustness curves, and removes the earlier trade-off and threshold-effect plots. Existing heatmaps are retained and relabeled.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful cost modeling, a better-aligned Zhang & Evans comparison, medical precision/recall, and scalability limitations. However, its new robust-cost evidence contains an unexplained inconsistency: for a fixed single-target cost, Definitions 4.1/4.3 imply cost decreases as Robcs increases, yet Table 1 gives SmoothAdv-CS both higher robustness and higher cost than Gaussian-CS (80.4%, 0.31 versus 72.3%, 0.08). Together with removal of the averaged ± summary and direct trade-off plots, this prevents a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
